# Executive summary {.unnumbered}

Harvest and clarification recovers A-Mab from the production bioreactor and delivers a
clarified, filtered feed to Protein A capture. Cells and cell debris are separated from the
culture fluid by continuous disk-stack centrifugation. The fine debris and colloidal material
the centrifuge passes are then removed on depth filters, and the clarified harvest is passed
through a sterilising-grade filter before capture. The step forms no quality attribute of the
antibody and no clearance of any impurity is claimed for it. What the step decides is the
condition of the load presented to Protein A chromatography.

This report presents the characterization of the step on a qualified scale-down model, executed
against the plan PCP-004. The scope came from the pre-characterization risk assessment RA-001,
which found no parameter of this step with a credible route to a critical quality attribute and
assigned all of them to univariate assessment. The step has `{python} n_params` process
parameters and all of them were carried into the study. Centrifugal field was studied between `{python} n0(p_cent.prange[0])` and
`{python} n0(p_cent.prange[1])` g, depth filter load between `{python} n0(p_load.prange[0])` and
`{python} n0(p_load.prange[1])` `{python} LOAD_UNIT`, and post-clarification turbidity between
`{python} ng(p_turb.prange[0])` and `{python} ng(p_turb.prange[1])` NTU. No designed multivariate
experiment was performed and none is claimed.

At the set-point the step recovered `{python} pct(hv_yield)` of the product mass entering it,
which is `{python} n0(mass_out_g)` g of `{python} n0(mass_in_g)` g, and delivered a clarified
harvest at `{python} ng(hv_turb_ntu)` NTU. No quality attribute of the antibody changed
measurably across the step at any setting studied. Host cell protein and residual DNA in the
clarified harvest were the burden the culture delivered, and the harvest operation neither
added to that burden nor cleared it within the precision of the assays. Raising the centrifugal field removes
more debris and shears more cells, and only the first of the two appeared. Centrate turbidity
fell as the field rose, and host cell protein in the clarified harvest did not rise at any field
up to `{python} n0(p_cent.prange[1])` g.

Of the `{python} n_params` parameters, `{python} n_kpp` were classified as key process
parameters and `{python} n_gpp` as a general process parameter. No parameter of this step is
critical. Neither the centrifugal field nor the depth filter load changed host cell protein,
residual DNA or aggregate in the clarified harvest at any setting studied. The normal operating ranges are unchanged from the ranges used
for clinical manufacture and each sits inside the range characterized here.

During execution `{python} len(dev_facts(DOC))` deviations were recorded. One was a pre-use
filter flush turbidity above its alert level, and one was a post-clarification turbidity excursion above the
normal operating range on a single run at high depth filter loading. Both were investigated,
both were dispositioned as retained, and neither affected product quality. The second is the
clearest single piece of evidence in this study for the mechanism the step is controlled on.

The step contributes to the control strategy through two key process parameter ranges,
in-process turbidity monitoring on every batch, depth filter media lot qualification, and the
turbidity condition the clarified harvest must meet before it is loaded onto Protein A. This
report rolls up into the master report PCMR-001.

# Introduction

## Product and unit operation

A-Mab is a humanized IgG1 monoclonal antibody produced in a fed-batch mammalian cell culture and
purified on a platform train that Novacyte Biologics has operated for three earlier products
[@amab2009]. The drug substance process runs from the production bioreactor through harvest,
Protein A capture, low-pH viral inactivation, cation exchange, anion exchange, small-virus
retentive filtration and ultrafiltration with diafiltration, and @fig-flow shows the train with
the principal quality impact of each step. The commercial process operates at
`{python} n0(scale_l)` L working volume, and the characterization reported here was performed on
a scale-down model of that operation.


Harvest and clarification is `{python} STEP` of that train. The culture fluid leaving the
production bioreactor is fed continuously to a disk-stack centrifuge, which sediments cells and
the larger cell debris under a centrifugal field. The centrate still carries fine debris,
colloids and nucleic acid fragments that are too small to sediment at an industrial feed rate.
That material is removed on a train of positively charged depth filters, and the clarified
harvest is passed through a sterilising-grade filter into the capture step. The step is operated
under SOP-2005 and SOP-2006.

The step forms no quality attribute of the antibody. The glycan, charge-variant and aggregate
attributes are formed in the production bioreactor and are reported in PCR-003. Host cell
protein and DNA clearance is credited to Protein A capture, cation exchange and anion exchange,
and is reported in PCR-005, PCR-007 and PCR-008. Viral clearance is claimed for the low-pH hold,
anion exchange and virus filtration, and no viral clearance is claimed for harvest. This step is
therefore characterized for what it delivers to the next step and for its recovery of product,
not for an attribute it sets.

![The A-Mab drug-substance process train, with the principal quality impact of each unit operation. Harvest and clarification is the primary recovery step between the production bioreactor and Protein A capture.](../outputs/figures/fig_process_flow.png){#fig-flow width=100%}

## Objectives

This study had five objectives.

1. Quantify the recovery of product across the step at its set-point and bound the variability
   of that recovery between batches.
2. Establish the range of each process parameter over which the clarified harvest remains
   acceptable as a feed to Protein A capture.
3. Confirm that no quality attribute of the antibody is formed, modified or cleared across the
   step within the ranges studied.
4. Classify each parameter of the step and give the reason for the class.
5. Provide the parameter ranges, the in-process monitoring and the feed conditions that the
   step contributes to the commercial control strategy.

## Regulatory and scientific basis

The study is a Stage 1 process design activity in the lifecycle approach to process validation
[@fda2011]. It follows the enhanced development approach of ICH Q8 and the quality risk
management principles of ICH Q9, and it supports the drug substance development and manufacture
described in ICH Q11 [@ichq8; @ichq9; @ichq11]. The process model, the quality attribute
framework and the risk-ranking method are taken from the A-Mab case study [@amab2009].

ICH Q9 treats criticality as a continuum rather than as a binary label. No parameter of this
step reaches the critical end of that continuum. @sec-classification gives the class of each
parameter and the evidence behind it.

# Prior knowledge and quality risk basis

## Platform and prior-product knowledge {#sec-prior-platform}

Centrifugation followed by depth filtration is the platform recovery operation at Novacyte
Biologics and has been used for X-Mab, Y-Mab and Z-Mab as well as for A-Mab clinical supply
[@amab2009]. The equipment, the media grades and the sequence of operations are common to all
four products. The accumulated experience shows that the operation is robust and that it does
not alter the product. The A-Mab case study reports the same for its own harvest step
[@amab2009]. This characterization therefore confirms and bounds the step, and it was not expected to
discover a new effect.

A higher centrifugal field raises the sedimentation velocity of cells and debris in proportion
to the field, so more of them reach the disk surface within the residence time of the bowl and
less passes into the centrate. The shear rate in the feed zone and at the disk stack also rises
with bowl speed, and cells damaged by that shear release intracellular protein and DNA into the
centrate. The parameter trades clarity against lysis, and the useful operating region
is the one where the first effect has saturated and the second has not yet started.

The depth filter has a finite capacity for solids and for the fine debris and colloids that the
centrifuge passes. Loading it further raises the pressure drop across the media, lets more fine
particulate and turbidity through as the media saturate, and at the extreme forces retained
material through the pores. Load per unit area, and not batch volume, is what tracks that
accumulation, because two batches of equal volume filtered through different installed areas
saturate the media to different extents.

Post-clarification turbidity is not set by the operator. It is a property of the clarified
harvest that the centrifugal field and the depth filter load produce, and it is a measure of the fine particulate
and colloidal material that the filters passed. It is carried in the parameter list because that
material fouls the Protein A column and shortens resin life, so a limit on it is a control on
the capture step rather than on this one.

Host cell protein and DNA in the clarified harvest are the reactor's burden plus whatever is
released by cells that break during the operation rather than in the reactor. Harvest does not
clear host cell protein. A gentle harvest keeps the load close to what left the reactor and a
harsh one adds intracellular protein to it. The depth filter media are positively charged and
adsorb a fraction of the DNA and debris the centrifuge passes, so some DNA removal across the
filtration stage is expected on mechanistic grounds. No clearance credit is taken for it, because the
adsorbed fraction is smaller than the qPCR assay can resolve against the spread of the feed
between runs.

Aggregate can rise at harvest only if the antibody unfolds at the shear rate of the centrifuge
feed zone or at an air-liquid interface created in a foaming transfer. Both exposures last
seconds. Any rise in aggregate across the step is therefore expected to be smaller than the SEC
method can resolve.

## Quality attributes in scope

The CQA register lists `{python} len(cqas_for(UO))` quality attributes as formed or controlled
at this step. The attributes in @tbl-cqa are the ones the clarified harvest carries into capture
and the ones the mechanisms above could change. They are
listed here as the attributes the study measured across the step, not as attributes this step
sets or clears. Criticality was assigned by the A-Mab Tool #1 assessment, which combines the
impact of the attribute on safety and efficacy with the uncertainty in that impact, and
attributes scoring high or very high are called critical [@amab2009].

```{python}
#| output: asis
show(cqas_by_keys(HARVEST_CQA_KEYS))
```

: Quality attributes measured across harvest and clarification, with their drug-substance acceptance criteria and criticality. None of them takes its value at this step. {#tbl-cqa}

Each of the three is in scope for a different reason. Aggregate is the most critical of the
three, and it is in scope because shear in the centrifuge feed zone can unfold the antibody and
drive it into soluble aggregate. Host cell protein is the attribute the condition of this step's
output bears on most directly, because cells that lyse under that same shear release
intracellular protein into the centrate and raise the load the capture column must clear.
Residual DNA is of very low criticality at the drug substance and is in scope because the
positively charged depth filter media adsorb DNA, and because DNA fragments and nucleosomes bind
to the filter matrix and to the capture resin and raise the pressure drop across both.

## Risk-based prioritization and parameter selection {#sec-risk-basis}

RA-001 ranked every parameter of the train by its potential impact on a critical quality
attribute and by its potential to interact with other parameters, and it used the resulting
score to assign a study type [@amab2009]. Parameters with a credible and interacting route to a
critical quality attribute were assigned to a multivariate design. Parameters with a route to process
performance, or with a route to a quality attribute that prior knowledge already bounds, were
assigned to univariate assessment. Parameters with neither were carried at their platform
ranges without new study.

For harvest and clarification the assessment placed all `{python} n_params` parameters in the
second group. The step has no mechanism by which it forms or removes a quality attribute of the
antibody, so the severity axis of the assessment is low for every parameter, and no interaction
between two parameters can raise a severity that is already low.

# Materials and methods

## Scale-down model and its qualification {#sec-sdm}

The characterization was executed on a scale-down model of the commercial harvest operation,
qualified under SOP-1001. The model comprises a laboratory disk-stack centrifuge of the same
disk geometry as the commercial machine and depth filter disks of the same media grades and the
same nominal retention ratings as the commercial filter train.

Two scaling rules define the model. The centrifuge is scaled on the ratio of volumetric feed
rate to the equivalent settling area of the bowl, which is the quantity that fixes the size of
the smallest particle a machine removes at a given throughput. Holding that ratio constant
between scales reproduces the clarification the commercial machine achieves, and it is applied
across the whole centrifugal field range studied here rather than at the set-point alone. The
depth filters are scaled at constant load per unit filter area, which is the parameter under
study and is by construction scale-independent. The feed zone geometry and the transfer
arrangement were reproduced at the wall shear rate of the commercial machine, because the feed
zone is where cells break and release intracellular protein into the centrate, and where the
antibody meets the highest shear rate anywhere in the step.

The qualification compared the model against commercial-scale data from the A-Mab engineering
campaign on centrate turbidity, clarified harvest turbidity, product recovery and the host cell
protein and DNA content of the clarified harvest. The comparison found no difference between
scales that the analytical methods could resolve. The model is therefore suitable for
establishing the operating ranges of this step, and the conclusions drawn on it are applied
directly to the commercial process.

Two bounds on the model apply to every result that follows. The model does not reproduce the residence time of product in the
commercial centrifuge bowl or the hold time of the clarified harvest before capture, and neither
was varied in this study. The model also uses filter disks rather than the commercial filter
modules, so pressure drop at a given load is representative of the media and not of the module
housing.

## Operation

The scale-down runs were operated in the commercial sequence. Culture fluid from the production
bioreactor was fed continuously to the centrifuge at the scaled feed rate and at the centrifugal
field under study. The centrate was collected and passed immediately to the depth filter train
at the load per unit area under study. The clarified harvest was then passed through a
sterilising-grade filter and held at the platform temperature until it was loaded onto the
capture column.

Inputs that the platform controls to a fixed specification were held at that specification and
were not varied. These include the media grade of the depth filters, the sterilising-grade
filter rating, the buffer used to flush the filter train before use, and the temperature of the
operation. They are identity and quality controlled under SOP-2006 and are not characterization
parameters. The feed to the step is the output of the production bioreactor and was taken at the
bioreactor set-point condition, so the impurity burden entering harvest was the burden that
PCR-003 reports for a set-point culture.

## Analytical methods

@tbl-sops lists the validated methods used. Turbidity was measured by nephelometry under
AMV-3015 on the centrifuge feed, the centrate and the clarified harvest, and it is the primary
in-process measure of clarification performance. Host cell protein was measured by ELISA under
AMV-3012 and residual DNA by quantitative polymerase chain reaction under AMV-3014, both on the
centrifuge feed and on the clarified harvest, so that any change across the step would appear as
a difference between two samples of the same batch. Size variants were measured by SEC-HPLC
under AMV-3011 on the same two samples, which is how the aggregate mechanism was checked.
Protein concentration was measured to close the mass balance.

@tbl-appa in Appendix A gives the performance of the two methods whose variance sets the
resolution of this study.

The turbidity method has a precision of `{python} ng(turb_rsd)` % relative standard deviation
and a limit of quantitation of `{python} ng(turb_loq)` NTU, and it contributes
`{python} pct(turb_var_frac)` of the total variance of a turbidity result. It resolves the
differences this study needed to see, since the set-point value of `{python} ng(hv_turb_ntu)` NTU
is an order of magnitude above the limit of quantitation. The host cell protein ELISA has a
precision of `{python} ng(hcp_rsd)` % relative standard deviation, which is the coarsest of the
methods used. A change in host cell protein across the step smaller than that is not detectable
by it. 

## Sampling plan

Each run was sampled at three points. A sample of the centrifuge feed was taken from the
bioreactor transfer line, a sample of the centrate was taken after the centrifuge and before the
depth filters, and a sample of the clarified harvest was taken after the sterilising-grade
filter. Turbidity was measured at all three points. Host cell protein, residual DNA and size
variants were measured on the feed and on the clarified harvest, which brackets the whole
operation.

Sampling at the centrate as well as at the clarified harvest separates the two stages of the
operation. A change in turbidity between feed and centrate is the work of the centrifuge, and a
change between centrate and clarified harvest is the work of the depth filters. Without the intermediate sample the two parameters could not be separated, because the
centrifuge and the depth filters both remove particulate and both removals appear in the same
turbidity result.

The set-point condition was run at the start and at the end of the study, so that any drift in
the model or in the assays over the execution period would be detected as a difference between
two nominally identical runs.

## Statistical methods

No model was fitted to the data of this study, because the study is univariate and no designed
multivariate experiment was performed. The analysis compares each condition against the
set-point condition, and it judges a difference by whether it exceeds the analytical variability
of the method that measured it. The precisions in @tbl-appa are the reference for that judgement. Where a difference did not exceed the precision of its method, the result is reported
as no detectable change and the bound is given as the precision of the method.

This convention is weaker than a fitted model with a lack-of-fit test. A univariate study
establishes the range of one parameter with the others held at their set-points. It cannot detect an interaction, where
the effect of one parameter depends on the level of another [@amab2009]. The consequence for
this step is bounded by the risk basis in @sec-risk-basis and is discussed in @sec-discussion.

Commercial-scale capability for the attributes reported in @sec-capability was estimated by
Monte Carlo simulation of `{python} f"{V['n_monte_carlo']:,}"` batches of the whole train, with
every parameter of every step drawn from within its normal operating range. Capability is
reported as a one-sided process capability index against the drug substance acceptance
criterion. The simulation varies every step of the train, so its
result is a property of the train.

# Study design

## Factors, ranges and the knowledge space

@tbl-params lists the parameters carried into the study with their set-points, normal operating
ranges and characterized ranges. The characterized range is the knowledge space explored in this
study and is not itself a proven acceptable range. The proven acceptable ranges are given in
@sec-par.

```{python}
#| output: asis
show(report_params(UO))
```

: Parameters of harvest and clarification, with set-points, normal operating ranges, characterized ranges, final classification and study type. {#tbl-params tbl-colwidths="[22,8,11,17,17,10,15]"}

The characterized ranges were set wider than the normal operating ranges on the same principle
the case study applies, which is that a range studied only to the edge of routine control cannot
show what happens when routine control is lost [@amab2009]. Centrifugal field was studied from
`{python} n0(p_cent.prange[0])` to `{python} n0(p_cent.prange[1])` g against a normal operating
range of `{python} n0(p_cent.nor[0])` to `{python} n0(p_cent.nor[1])` g. Depth filter load was
studied from `{python} n0(p_load.prange[0])` to `{python} n0(p_load.prange[1])` `{python} LOAD_UNIT` against a
normal operating range of `{python} n0(p_load.nor[0])` to `{python} n0(p_load.nor[1])` `{python} LOAD_UNIT`.
Post-clarification turbidity was studied from `{python} ng(p_turb.prange[0])` to
`{python} ng(p_turb.prange[1])` NTU against a normal operating range of
`{python} ng(p_turb.nor[0])` to `{python} ng(p_turb.nor[1])` NTU.

The depth filter load range has a direct engineering meaning at commercial scale. For a batch at
the commercial working volume of `{python} n0(scale_l)` L, the set-point load of
`{python} n0(p_load.setpoint)` `{python} LOAD_UNIT` sizes the filter train at about
`{python} n0(area_setpoint_m2)` `{python} AREA_UNIT` of media. The top of the characterized range corresponds to
about `{python} n0(area_at_load_max_m2)` `{python} AREA_UNIT` and the bottom to about
`{python} n0(area_at_load_min_m2)` `{python} AREA_UNIT`. The range therefore spans a factor of two in installed
filter area. Doubling the area halves the load each square metre carries and leaves the media
further from saturation at the end of the batch.

@fig-ranges shows each range with its normal operating range and set-point. The pattern is the
same for all three parameters. The normal operating range sits inside the characterized range
with margin on both sides, and the set-point sits inside the normal operating range.

```{python}
#| label: fig-ranges
#| fig-cap: "Characterized range (light band), normal operating range (dark band) and set-point (marker) for each parameter of harvest and clarification. The normal operating range sits inside the characterized range for all three parameters."
viz.apply_style()
fig, axes = plt.subplots(len(PARAMS), 1, figsize=(7.2, 3.6))
for _ax, _p in zip(axes, PARAMS):
    _lo, _hi = _p.prange
    _ax.barh([0], _hi - _lo, left=_lo, height=0.55,
             color=viz.SEQUENTIAL[1], edgecolor="none")
    _ax.barh([0], _p.nor[1] - _p.nor[0], left=_p.nor[0], height=0.55,
             color=viz.SEQUENTIAL[4], edgecolor="none")
    _ax.plot([_p.setpoint], [0], marker="D", ms=7, color=viz.INK, zorder=5)
    _pad = 0.10 * (_hi - _lo)
    _ax.set_xlim(_lo - _pad, _hi + _pad)
    _ax.set_ylim(-0.6, 0.6)
    _ax.set_yticks([])
    _ax.grid(False)
    _ax.set_xlabel(f"{_p.name} ({_p.unit})")
fig.tight_layout()
plt.show()
```

## Univariate characterization design

Each parameter was studied one at a time. The parameter under study was set in turn to the low
edge of its characterized range, to its set-point and to the high edge of its characterized
range, and every other parameter was held at its set-point. Intermediate settings were added for
depth filter load, because the mechanism is a saturation of the media rather than a linear
effect and the position of the change matters more than its size.

Post-clarification turbidity was not set at chosen levels, because no valve or drive controls
it. It takes the value that the centrifugal field and the depth filter load leave in the
clarified harvest. Its range was therefore covered by the settings of those two parameters that
produced turbidity across the characterized range, and the range recorded in @tbl-params is the
range of clarified harvest this study produced and assayed.

Every clarified harvest generated in the study was assayed for host cell protein, residual DNA
and size variants against the feed of the same run. The comparison is therefore within one batch
at every condition, which keeps the variability of the culture out of it.

## Verification at the set-point

The set-point condition was executed at the beginning and at the end of the study. Both
executions were assayed on the full panel. These runs serve two purposes. They bound the
variability of the step between batches at a fixed condition, which is the basis for the
recovery statement in @sec-setpoint. They also confirm that neither the scale-down model nor the
analytical methods drifted over the execution period, since a drift would appear as a difference
between two runs at the same condition.

# Results {#sec-results}

## Set-point performance and mass balance {#sec-setpoint}

@tbl-massbalance gives the mass balance and the clarification result at the set-point.

```{python}
#| output: asis
show(mass_balance_df)
```

: Product mass balance and clarification result across harvest and clarification at the set-point condition. {#tbl-massbalance}

The step recovered `{python} pct(hv_yield)` of the product mass presented to it. Of the
`{python} n0(mass_in_g)` g of A-Mab leaving the production bioreactor,
`{python} n0(mass_out_g)` g reached the capture step and `{python} n0(mass_loss_g)` g was not
recovered. The loss is accounted for by product held up in the sediment discharged from the
centrifuge and by product retained in the wetted volume of the depth filter train and its
housings. Both losses are volumetric. Installing more filter area to lower the load each square
metre carries therefore leaves more product behind in the wetted volume of the train.

Recovery at this step varies between batches with a coefficient of variation of
`{python} pct(hv_yield_cv)`, around an expected step yield of `{python} pct(hv_yield_base)`. The batch reported here
recovered above that expected value and within that dispersion. The cumulative yield of
the train through this step is `{python} pct(hv_cum_yield)`, and the whole train delivers
`{python} pct(V['overall_yield'])`. @fig-yield shows where the step sits in the cumulative yield of
the train.

![Cumulative product yield across the drug-substance train. Harvest and clarification is the first recovery loss after the production bioreactor.](../outputs/figures/fig_yield_waterfall.png){#fig-yield width=100%}

The clarified harvest at the set-point had a turbidity of `{python} ng(hv_turb_ntu)` NTU. That
value sits in the middle of the normal operating range of `{python} ng(p_turb.nor[0])` to
`{python} ng(p_turb.nor[1])` NTU and well above the limit of quantitation of the method, which is
`{python} ng(turb_loq)` NTU. The two set-point executions agreed within the precision of the
turbidity method. No drift of the scale-down model or of the assays was detected over the
execution period.

## Centrifugal field

Centrifugal field was varied from `{python} n0(p_cent.prange[0])` to
`{python} n0(p_cent.prange[1])` g with feed rate, depth filter load and every other input held at
the set-point. Turbidity of the centrate fell as the field rose.

The size of the effect is what decides the range. Across the field range studied, the
improvement in centrate turbidity was concentrated at the low end. Above the middle of the
range, further increases in field produced no further improvement in the clarified harvest that
the turbidity method could resolve. The interpretation is that the population the centrifuge can
remove has already been removed by then, and what remains in the centrate is the fine debris and
colloidal fraction whose sedimentation velocity is too low for the machine at any field it can
reach. That fraction is the depth filter's job, not the centrifuge's.

The lysis mechanism did not appear. Host cell protein and residual DNA in the clarified harvest
did not rise with field anywhere in the range studied. For host cell protein the bound is the
precision of the ELISA, which is `{python} ng(hcp_rsd)` % relative standard deviation, so the
result is that any increase in host cell protein caused by shear at the top of the range is
smaller than that. Shear damage to a cell population rises steeply once a threshold is passed, and the finding is that
`{python} n0(p_cent.prange[1])` g is below the threshold for this cell line at this feed rate.
The finding does not extend above the range studied.

Centrifugal field is therefore an effective parameter with a saturating benefit and no observed
penalty inside its characterized range. The normal operating range of
`{python} n0(p_cent.nor[0])` to `{python} n0(p_cent.nor[1])` g sits above the saturation point
of the benefit and below the onset of any detectable lysis.

## Depth filter load {#sec-depth-load}

Depth filter load was varied from `{python} n0(p_load.prange[0])` to
`{python} n0(p_load.prange[1])` `{python} LOAD_UNIT` with the centrifugal field at its set-point. The response
that moved is post-clarification turbidity, and it moved in the expected direction. Turbidity of
the clarified harvest rose with load, and the rise was not linear. Turbidity was flat across the
lower part of the range and rose over the upper part, which is the signature of a filter
approaching the capacity of its media rather than of a filter passing a constant fraction of
what it sees.

Solids accumulate on the media through the batch. As they do, the available media surface
falls, and particles that would have been captured early in a batch pass late in the same
batch.

The clearest single observation of this effect in the campaign came from a deviation rather than
from a planned run. On one run at a depth filter loading near the top of the range studied,
post-clarification turbidity reached `{python} ng(dev_004_02_turbidity_max_ntu)` NTU, which is
`{python} ng(turb_exceed_ntu)` NTU above the normal operating range ceiling of
`{python} ng(p_turb.nor[1])` NTU and `{python} n0(turb_exceed_pct)` % above it in relative terms.
The excursion is far larger than the `{python} ng(turb_rsd)` % precision of the turbidity method,
so it is a real excursion and not assay noise. The run reached that value with `{python} ng(turb_headroom_ntu)` NTU still remaining inside the
characterized turbidity range. @sec-dev-004-02 reports the deviation in full.

Host cell protein, residual DNA and size variants in the clarified harvest did not change with
load anywhere in the range studied. The depth filter media adsorb DNA, and a modest reduction in
DNA across the filtration stage is expected on mechanistic grounds, but no reduction large
enough to resolve against the assay was observed and no clearance is claimed.

The normal operating range of `{python} n0(p_load.nor[0])` to `{python} n0(p_load.nor[1])` `{python} LOAD_UNIT`
sits below the part of the characterized range where turbidity rises. The margin between the top
of the normal operating range and the top of the characterized range is the margin that absorbs
a filter train sized at nominal capacity running a batch of above-nominal volume.

## Post-clarification turbidity

Post-clarification turbidity across the study ran from `{python} ng(p_turb.prange[0])` to
`{python} ng(p_turb.prange[1])` NTU. That range was produced by the settings of the other two
parameters and was not imposed.

Turbidity matters to the next step and not to this one. The material it measures is fine
particulate and colloidal debris, and that material deposits on the head of the Protein A
column. The consequences are a rising column pressure drop over a resin lifetime and a slow loss of
dynamic binding capacity. None of these is a quality attribute of A-Mab. Each of them shortens
the number of cycles a resin lot runs before its dynamic binding capacity falls below the limit
set for the capture step. The limit on post-clarification turbidity is therefore set from resin
lifetime and not from a drug substance criterion.

Turbidity is also the only response in this study that moves usefully with either parameter, and
it is measured on every batch by a validated method with a precision of `{python} ng(turb_rsd)` %
relative standard deviation. It is therefore the natural in-process monitor for the step. A
turbidity result above the normal operating range indicates that accumulated solids have begun
to let fine particulate through the media. The run described in @sec-dev-004-02 is the case this
study observed.

## Product quality across the step {#sec-quality-across-step}

No quality attribute of A-Mab changed measurably across harvest and clarification at any
condition studied. Host cell protein, residual DNA and size variants were assayed on the
centrifuge feed and on the clarified harvest of every run. In every case the difference between
the two was within the precision of the method that measured it.

The bounds on that statement are the precisions themselves. For host cell protein the bound is
`{python} ng(hcp_rsd)` % relative standard deviation, which is the coarsest method in the panel,
and the limit of quantitation is `{python} ng(hcp_loq)` ng/mg. Any change in host cell protein
across the step that is smaller than the first of those numbers would not have been detected. For
residual DNA and for aggregate the bounds are the precisions of AMV-3014 and AMV-3011 as
established in their validation reports. Changes below these bounds are not excluded.

Two consequences follow. First, the impurity burden presented to Protein A capture is the
burden the culture delivered. It rises as culture duration lengthens and rises again as end of
culture viability falls, because both leave more lysed cells in the broth, and nothing done at
harvest moves it. PCR-003 reports those relationships. Second, this step takes no clearance
credit for any impurity and makes no viral clearance claim. The viral clearance claim
for A-Mab rests on the low-pH hold, anion exchange and virus filtration, and is consolidated in
PCMR-001.

No increase in aggregate was detected between the centrifuge feed and the clarified harvest at
any centrifugal field studied. The shear exposure in the feed zone of this operation is brief, and at
the fields studied it is not sufficient to unfold the antibody at a rate the SEC method can see.

# Design space

No design space is defined for harvest and clarification, and none is claimed. A design space is
a multivariate region over the parameters that govern a critical quality attribute, within which
the attribute is known to remain acceptable [@ichq8]. No critical quality attribute of A-Mab responds to a
parameter of this step, so there is nothing for such a region to be defined against, and the
multivariate studies that would define one were not performed.

What bounds this step instead is a set of univariate proven acceptable ranges, one per parameter,
supported by the data in @sec-results and reported in @sec-par. This is the distinction PDA
Technical Report 60 draws when it allows univariate approaches to establish a proven
acceptable range while reserving multivariate studies for the interactions between parameters.
The A-Mab case study excludes its seed expansion steps from the design space on the same ground
[@amab2009].

Movement inside the ranges in @tbl-par is movement inside a characterized region and is managed
under the site change management system [@ichq10]. Movement outside them requires assessment, and
because no multivariate model of this step exists, that assessment cannot be made by prediction.
It requires data.

# Proven acceptable ranges {#sec-par}

@tbl-par gives the proven acceptable range of each parameter with the basis on which it is
proven.

```{python}
#| output: asis
_par = report_params(UO)[["Parameter", "Unit", "Set-point", "NOR", "Char. range"]].copy()
_par = _par.rename(columns={"Char. range": "Proven acceptable range"})
_basis = {p_cent.name: "Clarification performance and product recovery",
          p_load.name: "Post-clarification turbidity and product recovery",
          p_turb.name: "Condition of the feed to Protein A capture"}
_par["Acceptance basis"] = _par["Parameter"].map(_basis)
show(_par)
```

: Proven acceptable ranges for the parameters of harvest and clarification, with the basis on which each range is proven. {#tbl-par tbl-colwidths="[18,7,11,16,18,30]"}

The proven acceptable range of each parameter is the range studied, because every condition
studied produced a clarified harvest that met the requirements of the next step and no condition
studied changed a quality attribute of the antibody. The value in the turbidity row is the turbidity the step
delivers when the other two parameters are at their set-points. Its range is an acceptance range
on the clarified harvest, and no operator moves it.

Three bounds apply to these ranges. Each was established with the other parameters held at their
set-points, so none of them is a statement about the corners where two parameters are at their
edges at once. Each rests on a scale-down model qualified against the attributes listed in
@sec-sdm, and the model bounds recorded there apply. Each is a range over which the step performs. None of them
is a range over which a critical quality attribute has been shown to remain in limit, because no
critical quality attribute of A-Mab responded to any parameter of this step.

The normal operating ranges in @tbl-par are narrower than the proven acceptable ranges in every
case, and they are unchanged from the ranges used for clinical manufacture. The margin between
the two is what absorbs normal equipment variability and measurement uncertainty at commercial
scale without leaving the characterized region.

# Process capability and robustness {#sec-capability}

Process capability is a property of a quality attribute and not of a process parameter. No
quality attribute of A-Mab takes its value at this step, so no capability is attributed to
harvest and clarification. @tbl-cap gives the commercial-scale capability of the three
attributes the clarified harvest carries into capture. Each of those values is produced by the
steps that clear the attribute.

```{python}
#| output: asis
show(cap_for(HARVEST_CQA_KEYS))
```

: Commercial-scale capability of the attributes carried forward from harvest, estimated by Monte Carlo simulation of the whole train with every parameter inside its normal operating range. The capability is delivered by the downstream steps that clear these attributes. {#tbl-cap}

Of the three attributes, `{python} tightest_cqa['CQA']` has the tightest capability at a process
capability index of `{python} f"{tightest_cqa['Cpk']:.3g}"`, and it is cleared by Protein A capture,
cation exchange and anion exchange as reported in PCR-005, PCR-007 and PCR-008. The tightest
capability anywhere in the drug substance is `{python} f"{V['min_cpk']:.2f}"` and it belongs to a
viral clearance attribute set at another step, which PCMR-001 consolidates.

The robustness of this step is its own recovery and its own clarification, and both were stable.
Recovery varied between batches with a coefficient of variation of `{python} pct(hv_yield_cv)` at
a fixed condition. Clarification performance was unchanged across the middle and upper part of the centrifugal
field range and across the lower part of the depth filter load range. The one condition at which performance degraded was high depth filter loading, and what
degraded was the turbidity of the clarified harvest. No attribute of the antibody changed with
it.

# Parameter classification {#sec-classification}

Parameters were classified under SOP-4001 using the decision logic of the A-Mab case study
[@amab2009]. A parameter whose variability affects a critical quality attribute is a critical
process parameter or a well-controlled critical process parameter, according to the risk that it
leaves its acceptable range. A parameter that affects process consistency or performance without
affecting a quality attribute is a key process parameter. A parameter with neither effect is a
general process parameter.

- Centrifugation (rcf) was classified as a key process parameter. A higher field removes more
  cells and debris and therefore leaves a smaller solids load for the depth filters to hold. No
  effect on any quality attribute was detected
  across `{python} n0(p_cent.prange[0])` to `{python} n0(p_cent.prange[1])` g, and in particular
  no shear-driven release of host cell protein or DNA was detected at the top of that range. The
  parameter is set on the machine and held by its drive control, so the risk of leaving the range
  is low.
- Depth filter load was classified as a key process parameter. Turbidity of the clarified
  harvest rises as loading rises, and the particulate that turbidity measures deposits on the
  head of the capture column and shortens the number of cycles the resin lot runs. No effect on
  any quality attribute was detected across `{python} n0(p_load.prange[0])` to
  `{python} n0(p_load.prange[1])` `{python} LOAD_UNIT`. Loading is fixed by the installed filter area and the
  batch volume, both of which are known before the batch starts, so the parameter is controlled
  by design rather than in real time.
- Post-clarification turbidity was classified as a general process parameter. It is an output
  of the step and not a setting, no quality attribute of A-Mab changes with it, and the
  particulate it measures deposits on the capture column, where the resin cycling limit bounds
  the consequence. It is
  measured on every batch under AMV-3015, where a result above the normal operating range
  identifies a batch whose depth filter media were loaded past the point at which they hold
  fine particulate.

Of the `{python} n_params` parameters, `{python} n_kpp` are key process parameters and
`{python} n_gpp` is a general process parameter. No parameter of this step is a critical process
parameter or a well-controlled critical process parameter. No quality attribute of the antibody
is formed or cleared at this step, and none responded to a parameter of it. Key process
parameters are included in the control
strategy even though they do not affect product quality, because controlling them keeps the
process consistent and predictable [@amab2009].

# Contribution to the control strategy

The step contributes four elements to the commercial control strategy.

The first is the two key process parameter ranges. Centrifugal field is controlled to
`{python} n0(p_cent.nor[0])` to `{python} n0(p_cent.nor[1])` g and depth filter load to
`{python} n0(p_load.nor[0])` to `{python} n0(p_load.nor[1])` `{python} LOAD_UNIT`, both inside the ranges proven
in @sec-par. Depth filter load is controlled by sizing the installed filter area for the batch
volume, which at the set-point loading is about `{python} n0(area_setpoint_m2)` `{python} AREA_UNIT` for a batch at
the commercial working volume.

The second is in-process monitoring. Post-clarification turbidity is measured on every batch
under AMV-3015 and is the in-process acceptance criterion the clarified harvest meets before it
is loaded onto Protein A capture. A result above the normal operating range sends the batch to
an assessment of its depth filter loading, because loading the media past their retention
capacity is what raised turbidity in the one run where turbidity rose.

The third is a life-cycle control on the equipment and the consumables. Depth filter media lots
are qualified before use by a pre-use flush with a turbidity acceptance criterion, which is the
control that detected DEV-004-01. Resin cycling limits at the capture step account for the
particulate the clarified harvest carries onto the column, and PCR-005 reports the cycling
limit.

The fourth is a specification on the load presented to the next step. Protein A capture
receives a clarified harvest with a defined turbidity range and a host cell protein and DNA
burden that rises with culture duration and with the fraction of cells that lysed before
harvest. PCR-005 characterizes the capture step on that load and not on an idealized one.

No release test of the drug substance depends on this step alone. The attributes in @tbl-cqa are
tested at the drug substance and are controlled by the steps that clear them. The contribution
of this step is consolidated in PCMR-001.

# Discussion {#sec-discussion}

The study confirms what prior knowledge predicted and bounds it with data. Harvest and
clarification recovers `{python} pct(hv_yield)` of the product presented to it, delivers a
clarified harvest at `{python} ng(hv_turb_ntu)` NTU at the set-point, and changes no quality
attribute of A-Mab within the ranges studied. What the step changes is the particulate and
impurity load that the capture column receives.

The mechanistic picture that emerges is a step operated comfortably inside two saturating
effects. The centrifuge is operated above the field at which its benefit saturates and below the
field at which shear damage to the cell population would begin, and neither edge was reached
inside the characterized range. The depth filter train is operated below the load at which the
media begin to saturate, and that edge was reached inside the characterized range and was
observed. One edge lies inside the studied region and one lies outside it, and the two statements
therefore do not carry the same confidence. The depth filter load limit is
supported by an observed transition. The centrifugal field limit is supported by the absence of a
transition, and that absence is bounded by the precision of the assays that looked for it.

Confidence in the scale-down model rests on the two scaling rules in @sec-sdm and on the
comparison against commercial-scale data. The residual risk is the shear rate in the feed zone, which a
laboratory centrifuge reproduces less faithfully than it reproduces clarification, and which is
what would break cells and unfold antibody if anything did. The study looked for the
consequence of shear directly, on every run, and did not find it.

Three limitations bound this report. The study is univariate, so it says nothing about the
corner where a low centrifugal field and a high depth filter load meet. That corner is the one
the mechanism predicts to be worst, because a poorly clarified centrate arriving at an already
heavily loaded filter train raises turbidity by both routes at once. The risk it carries is a
process performance risk and not a quality risk, and it is managed by controlling both parameters
independently within their normal operating ranges. The second limitation is that the
conclusions on host cell protein, DNA and aggregate are bounded by assay precision and not by
zero. The third is that hold time of the clarified harvest before capture was not varied, so this
report does not bound it, and it is controlled at the platform limit under SOP-2006.

Two deviations were recorded and both were retained. Neither affected product quality and neither
altered a conclusion of this report. One of them supplied the study's clearest observation of the
depth filter loading mechanism, reported in @sec-depth-load with the other observations and
again in @sec-deviations as a deviation.

# Conclusions

Harvest and clarification was characterized on a qualified scale-down model over the ranges in
@tbl-params, and the step performs as the platform experience predicted.

The step recovered `{python} pct(hv_yield)` of the product mass presented to it and delivered a
clarified harvest at `{python} ng(hv_turb_ntu)` NTU at the set-point. No quality attribute of
A-Mab was formed, modified or cleared across the step at any condition studied, and no clearance
credit and no viral clearance claim is taken for it. Proven acceptable ranges were established
for all `{python} n_params` parameters and are given in @tbl-par. No design space is defined for
this step, because no critical quality attribute of A-Mab responded to any parameter of it.

Of the `{python} n_params` parameters, `{python} n_kpp` were classified as key process
parameters and `{python} n_gpp` as a general process parameter. The step contributes two
parameter ranges, in-process turbidity
monitoring, depth filter media lot qualification and a defined feed condition for Protein A
capture to the commercial control strategy. During execution `{python} len(dev_facts(DOC))`
deviations were recorded, investigated and dispositioned as retained. The results of this report are consolidated
in PCMR-001.

# Deviations from the plan {#sec-deviations}

During execution `{python} len(dev_facts(DOC))` deviations from PCP-004 were recorded.
@tbl-dev lists them. Both were dispositioned as retained, which means that the affected data were
used as reported and that no run was repeated.

```{python}
#| output: asis

```

: Deviations recorded during execution of PCP-004. {#tbl-dev}

## DEV-004-01 — Depth-filter lot pre-use flush turbidity above alert

The pre-use flush of depth filter media lot LOT-DF-4408 gave a flush turbidity of
`{python} ng(dev_004_01_flush_turbidity_ntu)` NTU, above the alert level set for the flush in
SOP-2006. The lot was within its expiry date of `{python} lot_df_4408_expiry` and had been
released by the vendor against its own certificate. The deviation was detected at the flush
itself, before any culture fluid contacted the media.

The investigation attributed the result to an insufficient initial flush volume for this media
grade. Depth filter media shed a small quantity of fines when first wetted, and the flush volume
specified in SOP-2006 was found to be adequate for the grades in routine use but marginal for
this one.

The measurement is a pre-use measurement of the filter train, taken before product was present,
so no product was exposed to the fines that the reading reflects. Even at the flush value
observed, a clarified harvest at `{python} ng(dev_004_01_flush_turbidity_ntu)` NTU would have sat
inside the normal operating range for post-clarification turbidity, whose ceiling is
`{python} ng(p_turb.nor[1])` NTU. The lot was used and the data from the affected run were
retained. The investigation recommended that the minimum pre-use flush volume in SOP-2006 should
be stated per media grade rather than as a single value for the filter train.

## DEV-004-02 — Post-clarification turbidity excursion above the normal operating range {#sec-dev-004-02}

On one run at a depth filter loading near the top of the range studied, post-clarification
turbidity reached `{python} ng(dev_004_02_turbidity_max_ntu)` NTU. The normal operating range for
that attribute has a ceiling of `{python} ng(p_turb.nor[1])` NTU, so the excursion was
`{python} ng(turb_exceed_ntu)` NTU or `{python} n0(turb_exceed_pct)` % above it. The turbidity
method has a precision of `{python} ng(turb_rsd)` % relative standard deviation, so the excursion
is about `{python} n0(turb_exceed_vs_rsd)` times the analytical variability of the result and is
real. It was detected by
the in-process turbidity monitor under AMV-3015.

The investigation attributed the excursion to depth filter loading near the maximum of the
range under study, by the mechanism described in @sec-depth-load.

What rose was the turbidity of the clarified harvest, which measures the particulate carried to
capture. No attribute of the antibody rose with it. The host cell protein, residual DNA and
size-variant results for that run were within the precision of their methods against the feed of
the same run, and the turbidity itself stayed inside the characterized range, which extends to
`{python} ng(p_turb.prange[1])` NTU. The extra particulate the run carried onto the capture
column consumes part of the cycle life of the resin, and PCR-005 sets the cycling limit that
bounds it.

The run and its data were retained. The ceiling of the normal operating range for depth filter
load is set at `{python} n0(p_load.nor[1])` `{python} LOAD_UNIT`, below the loading at which that
run was executed.
